title.narrative: Life-saving integrated humanitarian assistance to address the most critical needs of returning IDPS and affected host communities in Kiremu Woreda, East Wollega Zone, Oromia region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtFIDO, ECDD, and Dorcas Aid Ethiopia propose a life-saving integrated humanitarian assistance to address the most critical needs of returning IDPS and affected host communities in Kiremu Woreda. Prolonged insecurity has caused large-scale displacement, infrastructure destruction, and loss of livelihoods in Kiremu woreda. The woreda hosts 13,869 IDPs and 48,983 returnees facing severe shortages of food, water, shelter, protection, health, nutrition and livelihood services, with women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities being particularly at risk. ltbrgtField assessments in October 2025 revealed that most displaced and returning families live in damaged or temporary shelters with limited access to safe water and sanitation, increasing risks of waterborne diseases and malnutrition. Health facilities are largely non-functional, and local authorities lack the capacity to meet growing humanitarian needs. Without urgent intervention, affected populations face worsening living conditions, disease outbreaks, and prolonged displacement. FIDO will lead Health, Shelter/NFI,and WASH interventions Dorcas Aid Ethiopia will lead Agriculture and ECDD will take the Multipurpose Cash (MPC) and ensure disability inclusion across sectors.ltbrgtIn the WASH sector, the project will improve access to safe water and sanitation for 29,376 people by solarizing an existing motorized deep well, rehabilitating a dug well, constructing WASH facilities at a health center, and conducting hygiene promotion activities. Health and nutrition interventions include mobile health teams providing primary healthcare, MISP, mental health and psychosocial support, immunization services, maternal and child health services, referrals, distribution of nutritional commodities and medical supplies, and malnutrition screening and treatment for children under five and pregnant or lactating women, reaching 20463 individuals.ltbrgtShelter/NFI assistance will deliver emergency shelter and essential household items to 500 vulnerable households, including 75 persons with disabilities. Agricultural assistance will provide improved maize seeds, farm tools, and input cash to 800 returnee households, and restock small ruminants for 100 HHs, mainly women-headed and persons with disabilities. MPC will disburse 28,800 ETB over three rounds to 162 returnee households, including 87 persons with disabilities, in line with Ethiopia’s minimum expenditure basket for the Oromia region. ltbrgtFurthermore, in collaboration with ECDD and DORCAS AID, training will be provided to project staff, community members, government officials, and project committees on PSEAH, AAP, targeting criteria, and Gender-Based Violence. Cross-cutting priorities, including gender equality, protection mainstreaming, conflict sensitivity, environmental safeguards, and accountability to affected populations (AAP), will be integrated into all project activities. Joint monitoring, review meetings, and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will be conducted. The project will adopt a community-centered and inclusive approach, ensuring the active participation of affected populations in assessment, planning, implementation, and monitoring processes.ltbrgtThe project was designed according to the needs on the ground, in consultation with relevant UN Clusters, ensuring complementarity with other projects funded by CERF/CBPF. Coordination will be maintained with zonal, regional, and national clusters (Agriculture, WASH, Health, Nutrition, Protection, ES/NFI, and CWG) and other humanitarian actors to ensure complementarity and alignment with the Ethiopia Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).ltbrgtThe project will directly and indirectly benefit approximately 93, 266 individuals, including IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host community members. Of these, about 52% will be women and girls, and 16% will be persons with disability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
